content:
deploy-bot: Starting canary rollout for release/2026-03-15 (ff: ff-new-routing) -> canary traffic 10% across us-east-1. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/release/canary-checklist :rocket:

devon: seeing a bunch of 5xx spikes from the canary group in the last minute. Not sure if it's infra or code.

pagerbot: Pager triggered: high_slo_burn - service=redwood-api environment=prod region=us-east-1 severity=page (count=120 in 1m) :rotating_light:

maya: I'm on it. devon, can you paste the alert fingerprint? Also is the canary dashboard loading?

devon: alert id 0x9f7c - attaching quick logs: request path /v1/generate, status 502/503. Tried to open /dash/prod/canary-latency but it's 404. The dashboard panel seems to be missing entirely.

ashley: I flipped ff-new-routing kill-switch in the console UI but the toggle returned a 500. Trying via API now.

infra-bot: API call failed: 500 from flags-service when writing flag ff-new-routing. Stack: 
```
PUT /api/flags/ff-new-routing
Status: 500
Body: {"error":"write-timeout","trace":"a1b2c3"}
```

maya: ok — two related problems: (1) observability gap - canary-specific panels removed in last dashboard refactor, (2) flag kill endpoint is overloaded (503s) because of a migration. We need immediate mitigation path.

sre-lead: devon, can you pivot traffic away from the canaries at the routing layer? If the flag toggle is flaky we can adjust ALB weight.

devon: yes, doing that now. Running: 
```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:... --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","TargetGroupArn":"tg-prod-primary","Weight":100}]'
```

deploy-bot: Canary traffic moved to 0% (confirmed). New traffic routed to stable pool.

luis: quick sanity check on customer impact - SLO dashboard shows a huge % burn because the alert aggregates global request count and the canary had tiny baseline. Ops team, we should avoid comparing absolute burn across tiny buckets.

maya: good catch. The alert/threshold uses "error_rate > 1% over 1m" with numerator from canary only but denominator pulled from global requests. That produced a massive-looking burn for a small absolute number of requests.

ashley: kill-switch API eventually accepted the request after a retry. Response: 200 ok. But we already shifted traffic.

devon: customers: we saw ~0.3% of total requests affected, mostly 502s localized to us-east-1 canary subset. Peak lasted ~8 minutes. No major downstream incidents confirmed by support.

pagerbot: Alert auto-resolved (high_slo_burn) after traffic change and kill-switch.

maya: post-incident notes from here:
- Immediate: rollback/route shift completed, kill-switch toggled as backup.
- Root cause (hypothesis): a regression in new-routing path combined with metrics/dashboard refactor that removed canary-specific visibility and an overly-global SLO aggregation rule.
- Observability gaps: missing canary panels (dashboard variable rename), alert uses mismatched numerator/denominator. Causes noisy pages and SLO confusion.

infra-bot: filed bug: INF-2031 "dashboard: restore canary panels and fix variable mapping". Link: https://issues.redwood/INF-2031

sre-lead: action items (owners):
- maya: add canary-specific SLO and fix alert aggregation logic (fix by EOD)
- ashley: verify flag-service migration health and add retry/backoff for kill toggles (PR in flight)
- devon: add quick-runbook step for ALB weight flip (short doc)
- eng-obsv: restore missing panels and add a dashboard smoke test to CI

luis: I'll coordinate customer comms if support needs to notify. Based on metrics, impact low, but we should be transparent.

maya: creating an incident entry and scheduling a 30m postmortem tomorrow. Please add logs/traces to the incident page.

devon: quick ops note: we should not route canary errors into the global SLO burn alert - it's noise. Proposed: compute canary and global SLOs independently and only page when absolute requests > X or impact > Y%.

ashley: PR opened for flag-service retry; test coverage added for 500->retry path. Link: https://git.redwood/flags/PR/452

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-4722 (canary rollout - missing observability + noisy alert) assigned to maya.

maya: thanks everyone. Closing the page — still monitoring for any lingering traces. We'll follow up in the postmortem with concrete remediation timelines. :white_check_mark:

devon: monitoring shows 0 errors for 10m. Good to close.

sre-lead: closing thread, moving action items to the incident board.
